The four mismatches are consistent with the **pre-existing synthetic-ctid fallback**, not a new candidate TID algorithm. They remain PG parity failures.

At `e686696add25112c0d2ce33720bd84f0e04e21bf`:

- [BuildSizes::finish](/home/meszmate/worktrees/roll/t3-d62e3d3b/crates/pg-engine/src/exec/rowsize.rs:239) resolves the selected row through [row_tid](/home/meszmate/worktrees/roll/t3-d62e3d3b/crates/pg-engine/src/exec/dml.rs:906): stored TID → heap-model TID → [ctid_of key hash](/home/meszmate/worktrees/roll/t3-d62e3d3b/crates/pg-engine/src/exec/scan.rs:153).
- The estimated fixture exceeds its 500-version limit. Model removal and subsequent unstamped rows leave the late ASC winner (`g=600`) and INCLUDE winner (`g=6000`) using the hash fallback. DESC selects the earlier `g=300`, whose stored TID can survive model removal. **Estimated does not imply every row has a synthetic TID.**
- Serial and parallel builds select the same data key and call the same resolver. Exact full-error agreement can therefore coexist with physical PostgreSQL TID divergence.

`row_tid`, `modelled_tid`, and `ctid_of` function bodies are byte-identical across e686, parent `fe7b0023c9df19a6dae1e6067ba8454998db48c5`, models `c66a076833291eaad99bdcfa7ed885ed2a68cb2c`, and index `483b4d6e5d41e9025aaa518d5774abd7971f4204`. Index483 already used `row_tid` in deferred size-error reporting.

The fallback and model-dropping mechanics are documented in source comments. That documents an existing limitation; it does **not** establish an accepted exemption from physical-TID parity. No expectations should change. The [cached report](/home/meszmate/.cache/pg-engine-resume-20261104/combined-pg18-oracles-r2/REPORT.md) correctly retains all four failed comparisons.

Existing command mapping, **not executed here**:

- **P6/P7:** `GOLDEN_FILTER=a163_index_row_size cargo test -p pg-engine --test golden -- --nocapture` — expression/partial and non-btree behavior; lacks required dispatch/worker trace proof.
- **P8:** `cargo test -p pg-engine --test big_tables parallel_index_builds` and `cargo test -p pg-engine --test models_kept` — related parity coverage; does not establish immediate modeled layout before VACUUM with actual-worker evidence.
- **P9:** `cargo test -p pg-engine --test big_tables deferred_model_matches` — related bulk-write/TID coverage; no exact existing test closes the in-transaction CREATE INDEX obligation.
- **P10:** `PGISOLATION_ONLY=roll-index-progress cargo test -p pg-engine --test pg_isolation -- --ignored --nocapture` — progress/cancellation coverage uses expressions and serial fallback. Successful worker scan accounting remains open.
- **P11/P12:** `GOLDEN_FILTER=a163_review_concurrent cargo test -p pg-engine --test golden -- --nocapture` — existing formation/INVALID/retry coverage addresses P11 narrowly; P12’s additional deferred2704/GIN/expression cases remain uncovered.

Measured parbuild’s raw/detoasted heap packing also predates this candidate: fe7 lines121/128 feed raw sizes into `heap_pages`; c66 retains that behavior. It belongs to the separate **measured-parbuild/root-TOAST repair lane under parent coordination**. Neither the modeled validator repair nor Load/VACUUM repairs close it.

Read-only assessment only. No files, refs, targets, expectations, or services changed; no tests or builds run. Parent-reported e686 passes do not close these remaining parity and coverage limits.
